author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This function computes the **"reverse degree"** of a lowercase string by giving every letter a reversed alphabet value and weighting it by its position. It loops over each character `s[i]` and takes its ASCII code with `s.charCodeAt(i)`; since `'a'` is `97` and `'z'` is `122`, subtracting the code from `123` maps `'a'` to `26`, `'b'` to `25`, and so on down to `'z'` mapping to `1`, effectively reversing the alphabet. That reversed value is then multiplied by the **1-based position** of the character, `(i + 1)`, so letters later in the string contribute more. Each product is added to the running total `res`, which is returned at the end as the final degree. The whole thing runs in a single pass, so it is **O(n)** time and **O(1)** extra space.
